subject: Side effects of plotting with marginal effects

messages.author: 245e97a78d1b3640
messages.subject: Side effects of plotting with marginal effects
parts:
I'm getting a kind of weird side effect from plotting with marginal_effects. 

Say I do something like

# load the file
colors <- c(mode = "black", extreme = "red", marginal = "gray")
figdata <- readRDS("e1freq-fullmodel-gabor.rds")

# model the marginal effects
me <- marginal_effects(figdata, effects="label_relevant:label_incidental")

# extract the first object and append ggplot stuffs
g2 <- plot(me)[[1]] +
  xlab("Relevant label") + ylab("Rating") +
  labs(title = "Experiment 1 Frequency Ratings", colour = "Incidental label", fill = "Incidental label") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
  theme_tufte(myfontsize, ticks = F, base_family = myfont) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.5), axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 1), legend.position = "top", panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "white"))

g2

One would expect this to output one plot. But it outputs two. I've found that in the process of assigning the raw output (what is supposedly just a ggplot object) from "plot(me)[[1]]", some kind of side effect occurs outputting the unstyled plot to whatever output device happens to be listening at the time. This means if I call the above code in a knitr document it spits out two plots, one unstyled and one styled. 

I feel like I'm missing something and it probably has nothing to do with brms, but I figured I'd ask because someone might have encountered this behavior here before. Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Side effects of plotting with marginal effects
parts:
If you want to customize ggplot objects and avoid automatic plotting of marginal_effects, go for

plot(me, plots = FALSE)[[1]]
